propositions: Mirror Guard replication check exits 1 on a single instantaneous divergence sample during normal post-submit lag, causing false-positive red runs when the next scheduled run (within 16 minutes) passes.

The module's docstring (commit d96628c9dca) documents that transient divergence is expected and the alarm layer must absorb it via a sustained-divergence evaluation window, but the workflow entry point runs only one sample with no lag tolerance.

The secondary CloudWatch watcher implements the designed 2×5-min sustained-divergence window correctly; the primary workflow watcher (.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml) has no corresponding evaluation window.

The fix adds an in-process, portable `replication_check_with_lag_tolerance()` wrapper that re-samples on divergence up to 3 attempts over ~90 seconds; it returns healthy if any sample converges and unhealthy only if divergence persists across the window.
GitHub-ahead or foreign divergence never converges to Gerrit SHA and remains unhealthy on every run; missing SHA on first sample fails immediately without re-sampling.

The solution maintains strict no-weakening semantics: today's failure set minus only the transient lag that converges within the window, with CLI flags (--lag-attempts, --lag-delay-seconds) for tuning.
